Looking at the training examples:
Example 1:
- Input has color 3 and color 4.
  Color 3 is on the left / top:
  Row 2: cols 5..10 (length 6)
  Row 3: col 5 (3), cols 8..11 (4)
  Row 4: col 5 (3), cols 8..11 (4)
  Row 5: col 5 (3), cols 8..11 (4)
- Notice the shape: Color 3 is like the top and left edges of a rectangle or a symmetric shape, but color 4 overlaps or is an intruder?
Wait, look at the output of Example 1:
  Row 2: 3 at cols 5..10
  Row 3: 3 at col 5, 3 at col 10
  Row 4: 3 at col 5, 3 at col 10
  Row 5: 3 at col 5, 3 at col 10
Wait! Color 3 was:
Row 2: [5..10]
Row 3: [5]
Row 4: [5]
Row 5: [5]
It's symmetric! If it is symmetric around the vertical line col = 7.5 (between 7 and 8),
Col 5 reflects to Col 10!
Row 2 has cols 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 -> perfectly symmetric!
And the block of 4s: cols 8..11, rows 3..5. The 4s were completely removed, but why is there a 3 at col 10?
Because of vertical reflection symmetry!
The color 3 shape is made symmetric!
Wait, in Example 2:
Look at color 6:
Row 2: col 7
Row 3: col 6, (col 8 has 2)
Row 4: col 5, 6, 7, (col 8, 9, 10 have 2)
Row 5: col 4, 5, 6, 7, (col 8, 9, 10 have 2)
Row 6: col 5, 6, 7, (col 8, 9, 10 have 2)
Row 7: col 6, (col 8 has 6)
Row 8: col 7
The center of symmetry is column 7!
In row 3: col 6 -> reflected across col 7 is col 8!
In row 4: cols 5, 6, 7 -> reflected across 7 are 7, 8, 9!
In row 5: cols 4, 5, 6, 7 -> reflected across 7 are cols 7, 8, 9, 10!
In row 6: cols 5, 6, 7 -> reflected across 7 are cols 7, 8, 9!
In row 7: col 6, col 8 (already symmetric!)
In row 8: col 7.
And color 2 is completely replaced/removed! It was occupying cols 8, 9, 10 in rows 3..6.
Wait, why was color 2 there? It's like an occluder! Or color 4 in Example 1 was an occluder!
Color 4 (or 2) covers the shape or is an obstacle/occluder that got removed, and the primary shape is made symmetric (or the occluded half of the symmetric shape is restored).

Let's check the test input to be certain.
